findings.title: The good reward becomes the abiding domain
findings.claim: The focus phrase can make the promised good reward itself the inhabitable domain of permanent abiding: the believers remain forever within the good recompense named in 18:2.
findings.mechanism: The bound focus pronoun in فِيهِ resumes the adjacent masculine singular أَجْرًا حَسَنًا, while مَّٰكِثِينَ and أَبَدًا supply settled residence and unbounded continuation; the reward therefore becomes an experienced domain rather than an unspecified 'there'.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear فِيهِ as a domain with content and inhabitation, not merely as a location left unnamed by the translation.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains 'they will remain there forever'. The antecedent assignment is attributed contextual evidence, and the packet leaves an elliptical garden or outcome as a live alternative; no specific afterlife geography is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and 18:2 Arabic are supplied, but the HFT identity is legacy_unbound and the contextual branch records for reward and goodness have no independent registry descriptors.
